Roofing in Waxahachie, Texas

Waxahachie mixes Gingerbread-era houses near the courthouse with new subdivisions on its edges, and the roof rules are not the same for both. Call one free number any hour to reach an independent roofing company that serves Waxahachie.

Call (469) 649-7066 Historic district roofs

  2. Service Areas
  3. Waxahachie

Two kinds of Waxahachie roofs

Waxahachie is the county seat of Ellis County and has carried the nickname "Gingerbread City" for the Victorian houses built during its boom years in the late 1800s and early 1900s. Its Richardsonian Romanesque courthouse still anchors downtown, and the West End Historic District, listed on the National Register in 1986, covers 77 acres of Queen Anne and Classical Revival buildings.

That is only half the city. The 2020 census counted 41,140 people, and the city's community profile estimated 53,000 as of June 1, 2026, which means thousands of newer homes on the edges of town. A roof on a 1990s ranch or a new subdivision house is a straightforward job. A roof on a turreted Victorian near the courthouse can bring historic review into the picture.

DFW Expert Roofers does not do either job. It is a free line answered by an automated assistant around the clock. Tell it you need roofing, describe the house and the problem, and it transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that serves Waxahachie.

Roofing a house in a Waxahachie historic district

The city's historic preservation pages set out when the Heritage Preservation Commission gets involved. Here is how that plays out on a roof.

When a certificate is required

Under Section 24-56 of the city code, a Certificate of Appropriateness is required for alteration, restoration or new construction in a historic overlay district. The same review covers National Register properties and designated landmarks.

When a roof counts as maintenance

The city's historic tax incentive guidance lists roof replacement among routine maintenance that preserves a property without altering its historic appearance, and says routine residential maintenance does not need a certificate. Like for like is the safe reading.

When it becomes an alteration

Changing the roofing material, the color family, the roofline or adding features such as skylights changes how the house looks from the street. Ask the city before you sign a contract that includes any of those.

What skipping review can cost

For owners in the Historic Property Tax Incentive Program, the city says work completed without prior approval, however good the work, disqualifies the property from the program for that year.

Old houses also hide surprises a new subdivision home does not: multiple past layers, plank decking, chimneys with tired flashing and roof slopes that change across the house. Ask the roofer how it will inspect those before pricing the job.

Roofing work Waxahachie owners ask about

Requests range from a leak at an old chimney to a full replacement after hail, plus questions about metal roofs on rural property outside town.

Permits and paperwork at City Hall

  1. Call Building Inspection first. Waxahachie's building inspection staff answer at 469-309-4020. Ask whether your roof job needs a permit and, if the house is in a historic overlay district, whether planning staff need to see it.
  2. Check the roofer's registration. The city's permitting page includes a contractor registration form, which asks for the owner's driver license and proof of liability insurance of at least $300,000. Ask the roofer whether it has registered with Waxahachie.
  3. File through the CSS portal. The city takes applications, payments and inspection requests through its online Citizen Self Service portal.
  4. Expect the 2021 codes. Waxahachie adopted the 2021 International Codes, effective June 1, 2024. The city's own building guide repeats the code rule that asphalt shingles go only on slopes of 2:12 or steeper, with double underlayment on slopes from 2:12 to 4:12, which matters on porch roofs and additions with a low pitch.
  5. Keep the record. Hold on to the contract, any permit, the final invoice and the shingle warranty registration. On a historic home, keep any certificate as well.

The Saturday a tornado hit the new high school

Waxahachie High School had been open only since August when storms rolled through on Saturday, October 13, 2018. The National Weather Service confirmed a high-end EF-0 tornado that touched down just southwest of the school, with peak winds estimated near 85 mph in NOAA's storm record. Windows shattered, a door was busted, parking lot lights were bent and an old band bus ended up upside down in a nearby field. About 25 theater students were inside for a workshop, and no one was hurt.

An EF-0 is the weakest rating on the scale, yet it was enough to wreck a brand new building's doors and glass. On houses, winds in that range peel shingles and ridge caps and throw debris onto roofs. After any storm, look from the yard and from inside, and keep off the roof.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Why people in Waxahachie call the line

  • A leak in an old house. Chimneys, valleys and porch tie-ins on century-old homes are common leak points, and owners want someone who will look before quoting.
  • Hail on a newer subdivision roof. Owners on the growing edges of town want the damage documented clearly before they talk to the adjuster.
  • A historic home and a material question. Whether to keep shingles, switch to metal or match what is there, and how the city's review affects the choice.
  • Not knowing who to trust. After storms, out-of-town crews knock on doors. Callers would rather reach a locally owned company and check its city registration.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

A drip by the chimney of an old Victorian, or hail bruises on a five-year-old roof? Call and describe the house. A roofing company that works in Waxahachie takes it from there with an in-person look and its own written price.

Waxahachie roofing questions

Do I need city approval to replace the roof on a historic home in Waxahachie?

Ask the city first. Waxahachie requires a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Heritage Preservation Commission for alteration, restoration or new construction in a historic overlay district, on National Register properties and on designated landmarks. The city's tax incentive guidance treats a roof replacement that keeps the historic look as routine maintenance that does not need one. A change in material, color or roof shape is a different matter, so check before ordering anything.

Which Waxahachie roofing companies can I call after a storm?

This line does not publish a list or rank companies. Call the number on this page, say you need roofing, and an automated assistant connects you with an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Waxahachie calls. Ask that company for its city contractor registration, an insurance certificate and a written scope, and compare it with other bids. The roofer checklist explains each item.

Does Waxahachie have a contractor registration?

The city's permitting page offers a contractor registration form alongside its permit submittal guides, and permits are filed through the city's online CSS portal. Building Inspection, at 469-309-4020, can tell you what your roof job needs and whether the roofer you hired is on file. Ask before the old roof comes off, not after.

Is a metal roof allowed on an older house in Waxahachie?

Outside the historic overlay districts, ordinary building codes apply. Inside them, or on a National Register property or local landmark, a switch from shingles to metal changes the appearance of the house, which is the kind of alteration the Heritage Preservation Commission reviews. Talk to the city's planning staff early. The metal roofing page covers the material itself.

Roof trouble in Waxahachie? Call the free line

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.
